reciprocal.why: A cross-tradition pairing: the Daoist wu wei, effortless and unforced activity, and Heidegger's release from willing.
An editorial comparison between Buddhist clinging (upādāna) and Eckhart's letting go of attachment to one's actions.
The SEP calls Eckhart's negative virtues Stoic-sounding, which is why the compendium pairs them with the Stoic freedom from passion.
The beginner's mind is empty of the expert's habits and open to possibilities; Heidegger's waiting expects nothing and holds no object.

In ACT, acceptance is the active and aware embrace of private experiences without unnecessary attempts to change their frequency or form; Gelassenheit is a release of willing. The compendium treats them as neighbours, not the same thing.
Dogen's just sitting and Heidegger's 'nothing but wait' are paired by the compendium as contemplative neighbours.
The helplessness response is what malleability beliefs are read against: growth mindset research grew from attribution studies of helpless versus mastery-oriented responses.
Mastery-oriented persistence is the response pattern associated with malleability beliefs; helplessness is its counterpart.
The belief that ability grows and the practice that grows it are two sides of developable skill.
Both are belief constructs built on attribution research: what failure and setbacks are taken to mean.
Maintenance begins where formation ends: keeping a habit going once automaticity has plateaued.
Stacking is context-cue design for formation: anchoring the new behaviour to an existing routine.
Habit formation is the process the Wood-Neal context-cue model describes.
Everyday routines as habit chains are the applied-behaviour-analysis view of the same acquisition process.
Negative visualisation is the modern cognitive name for the Stoic premeditation of evils.
Rehearsing misfortune and loving what comes are the two halves of the Stoic acceptance pair.
The reserve clause ("fate permitting") is the planning habit the premeditation trains.
The stream is James's name for the undivided flow that pure experience describes before reflection.
The specious present is the present field James calls pure experience.
Objectless sitting enacts the non-divided experience the page describes.
Bracketing suspends the subject-object split that pure experience precedes.
The beginner's open stance meets experience before it has been divided into expert categories.
Mind wandering is task-unrelated thought without rumination's depressive grip; the two are often conflated.
Self-transcendence names the orientation; the self-transcendent experiences are the episodic states it aims at.
Ego dissolution is the annihilational component of self-transcendence in its strong form.
Collective effervescence is the group-level version of connected self-loss.
The undivided field is what self-transcendent experience briefly restores.
Self-transcendence is the related self-surpassing idea without Nietzsche's power vocabulary.
Amor fati is Nietzsche's affirmative formula for what the will accepts.
Nihilism is the diagnosis the will to power answers.
Ressentiment is the reactive drive contrasted with the will to power.
Perspectivism is Nietzsche's companion epistemology.
Agape is love given without regard to worth; grace is the unearned favor it presupposes.
Kenosis, self-emptying, is agape's form in Christology.
Keeping no account of evil (1 Corinthians 13) is what forgiveness acts on.
Benevolence is the disposition agape names in its plainer form.
Unconditional positive regard is the psychological analogue of love without regard to worth.
Both theories explain emotion as arising after an interpretive step rather than from the event alone.
The somatic marker is the body-first route to the evaluation appraisal theory describes.
Affect labeling is putting the appraisal into words, and changes the emotion accordingly.
Broaden-and-build describes what positive emotions do once the appraisal comes back positive.
Ubuntu is the southern African relational account of the person; associated living is Dewey's relational account of democracy.
Civic republicanism treats participation as constitutive of freedom; associated living is the participatory mode Dewey describes.
Dialogue is the communication Dewey makes primary to conjoint experience.
Growth mindset is the belief side of Dewey's growth reading of ability.
Habit formation is the mechanism by which capacities are built over time.
Mastery orientation is the goal structure that keeps growth intrinsic.
Learning by doing is the pedagogical method of the growth view.
Inquiry over received answers belongs to the same Deweyan tradition.
Extrinsic motivation is the contrast case the definition of intrinsic motivation builds on.
The veil of ignorance is Rawls's device for choosing the principles of justice.
Care ethics is the relational tradition Justice's page marks via Held.
Restorative justice is the corrective branch of justice in its modern form.
Expressive writing is the writing intervention in the Pennebaker stream of meaning-making research.
Benefit finding is the positive-reappraisal outcome of meaning-making.
Mudita is the third of the four immeasurables.
Schadenfreude is the inverse of mudita: pleasure at another's misfortune versus joy at their fortune.
Experiential avoidance is the counter-construct psychological flexibility is defined against.
Acceptance alongside values-based action is the acceptance half of psychological flexibility.
Cognitive defusion is the looking-at-thoughts half of psychological flexibility.
Right intention is the second factor of the Eightfold Path.
Freedom from ill will, the resolve's second component, is the stance metta trains.
If-then plans are the modern goal-structure parallel to setting intention in advance.
Self-concordant goals pursue alignment with values, the parallel the compendium's motivation principles draw.
MN 9 defines the way of practice as the noble eightfold path, right view first; the concept page belongs to that training
the Kaccanagotta Sutta teaches right view via the middle using the dependent co-arising chain between the existence extremes
the factor that precedes intention in MN 9's list: right view, then right resolve, then right speech
another factor in MN 9's list of the way of practice
the attention principles label their Buddhist parallel 'The coloured lens (Buddhism, Right View)'
the Appraisal theory page already links B021's interpretation-first orientation; Right view is that orientation's home
the First impressions bias seed names Buddhism's Right View as its tradition
CO051's parallels list Right view (Buddhism, Eightfold Path) alongside the distortion patterns
that page already cites B021 among its parallels; Right view is the concept behind it
E035 and E067 cite the face and the look together; the Sartrean gaze and the Levinasian face are the compendium's two accounts of the other's eyes
A012's psychology parallel is labelled 'Urge surfing and acceptance-based regulation'; the two are the compendium's paired acceptance techniques
The wisdom page presents wise reasoning as one of the two main lines of wisdom research.
Aristotle's practical wisdom and modern wisdom research both concern judgment in practical affairs.
The Berlin paradigm is one of the two main research programs studying wisdom.
The Socratic knowledge of not knowing concerns the theme of intellectual humility that also appears in modern wisdom research.
The umbrella family of judgment-in-action concepts; wisdom research studies such judgment empirically.
Aggregating many judgments is a different route to good outcomes than one person's wise reasoning.
The Vajrayana parallel: afflictions ripened into wisdom rather than suppressed.
The emotional side of the wisdom construct family.
